PSA for anyone considering June Homes in NYC
My SO Jasmin Tran and I used June Homes for a long term sublet from January to November. While the apartment wasn’t in the best shape, the sublet allowed us to extend our 5 years in NYC before we moved back to be closer to our families.
In the beginning of September, we discovered rats in our apartments. We immediately filed a ticket with Junes Homes and escalated. June Homes took weeks to send an exterminator to our place, and after the exterminator plugged up several massive holes behind the stove and dishwasher, he told us that the wall structure was too thin and that rats could make new holes within a day. He said as long as the walls weren’t fixed, the root issue of the rats would remain.
We brought this up with June Homes and June Homes feigned ignorance before finally sending the SAME exterminator back to our apartment. The exterminator reconfirmed his findings, and we followed up with June Homes yet again. June Homes then proceeded to try to deflect the issue to the building management and management sent their own exterminator who just unsealed and resealed the same holes. After over a month of us escalating the issue, June Homes finally sent an inspector to check the walls. The inspector confirmed the walls were inadequate and that they couldn’t be fixed while we lived here.
June Homes then tried to offer us relocation to a different apartment even though we only had a month left on the sublet lease. They finally gave us a one-time $500 rent credit (despite rent being ~4000 a month) and closed the ticket.
During this whole time, we’ve had to deal with rats tearing open our sealed food and leaving their droppings. We’ve had to sleep over at multiple friend’s places as the living conditions have been too disgusting for us to be comfortable to be inside our own place.
This is by far the worst housing experience we’ve ever had and we regret getting this sublet so much. Please be careful when subletting with them!!!

Side hip pain at night usually isn't your hip joint. 
If the side of your hip aches when you lie on it, the cause is often the tendons on the outside of the hip (often labeled "hip bursitis"), not arthritis.
• Joint arthritis tends to ache in the groin. Tendon pain sits on the side of the hip.
• Lying on that side, or letting your top knee drop across, squeezes the tendon against the bone.
• Stretching your knee across your body can add more squeeze. Complete rest alone lets the muscles weaken.
• In the 2018 LEAP trial (BMJ), education plus exercise beat a steroid shot at 8 weeks, and the benefit held at one year.
 Try tonight: sleep on your good side with a pillow between your knees.
Calm the squeeze, load the muscles gradually, and give it a few weeks. Results vary, so get checked if it isn't improving.
